claim_boundary: A rising DEXJPUS rate means yen depreciation against the U.S. dollar and may proxy global carry risk appetite, but it is not a direct measure of leverage, funding or Bitcoin demand. Monetary-policy divergence, intervention and safe-haven flows can break the sign. This supports one audit only.

independence_and_duplicate_boundary.distinct_from_closed_broad_dollar: DEXJPUS is a bilateral yen carry and safe-haven axis, while the closed DTWEXBGS family used a trade-weighted broad-dollar change as DRA entry admission. Parent, comparator and causal mechanism differ.
independence_and_duplicate_boundary.distinct_from_closed_rates_and_financial: The feature reads only a lagged bilateral FX price and cannot use yields, inflation, NFCI, VIX, WTI, BTC price or on-chain state.
independence_and_duplicate_boundary.prohibited_rescue: Do not add other currencies, carry-rate differentials, BOJ or Fed decisions, intervention labels, broad-dollar indices, volatility, thresholds, smoothing, alternate horizons, inverse direction, fractional sizing or leverage after access.

adversarial_prior: USDJPY can rise because of U.S.-Japan policy divergence rather than broad risk appetite.
Official intervention and safe-haven demand can abruptly reverse the yen relationship.
Weekly aggregation and conservative release lag may discard faster information.
Present-vintage daily history does not prove original-release availability or absence of revision.
A long-cash rule can improve apparent safety only by forfeiting BTC upside.
